newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Confusion surrounds Brazzaville shooting outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Confusion surrounds Brazzaville shooting outbreak.

text.p: Sustained shelling and shooting broke out in the Congo Republic capital Brazzaville on Wednesday night but it was unclear whether it represented a breach of a fragile truce in force there.

One unconfirmed report suggested that the outburst might be celebrations linked to peace progress, with talks between representatives of President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor Denis Sassou Nguesso planned for Thursday or Friday.
Witnesses across the river in Kinshasa reported that the outburst lasted for more than half an hour.
Lissouba and former military leader Sassou put their names to the truce on Saturday. It took effect at midnight on Monday.
Brazzaville residents and aid workers said earlier that the truce two rivals had been "more or less respected" despite the occasional "very, very sporadic" burst of shooting.
Of numerous ceasefires declared since the bloody showdown between Lissouba and Sassou started on June 5, not one has been strictly adhered to.

Mohamed Sahnoun, the U.N. and Organisation for African Unity special envoy who met both sides in Brazzaville on Tuesday, said afterwards representatives of both sides could meet in Gabon's capital Libreville late Thursday or early Friday.

Gabonese President Omar Bongo is the international mediator in the conflict, which began after soldiers surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militias ahead of a now postponed July 27 presidential election.
Sahnoun has said the aim is to secure conditions to enable a presidential election to be held within the next two months. Plans for a U.N.-sponsored mainly African peace force are taking shape.
Medical workers say the political and ethnic clashes have killed hundreds of people in the capital of the oil-producing former French colony, many of them civilians.
French troops evacuated almost 6,000 foreign nationals.
